deed: לוי יששר ואב-הטיפוס של דוד השמש
title: Levi Yissar built a solar water heater in his home, founded Neryah in 1953, and the heater went up onto Israel's roofs

trailer.text: Levi Yissar was an Israeli engineer and entrepreneur who, in the 1950s, proposed that instead of building more power plants, homes in Israel should switch to heating water with the sun.
According to Green Prophet, Levi Yissar, an engineer and entrepreneur, is the Israeli pioneer and innovator who had the idea that the sun’s power could be harnessed.
According to WhyAliyah, in the 1950s there was a fuel shortage in Israel, and the government forbade heating water between 10:00 and 18:00.
According to WhyAliyah, Yissar built a prototype solar water heater in his home, and in 1953 he founded the NerYah Company, Israel's first commercial manufacturer of solar water heaters.
The heater was placed on the roof and connected by pipes to two glass-faced collector plates, and the hot water was stored in it for the kitchen and the bathroom.
According to Green Prophet, in 2009 most private homes and small apartment buildings in Israel had solar water heaters.

stations.title: A new state without enough energy

paragraphs.text: According to Green Prophet, in the early 1950s electricity was very expensive because of a severe energy shortage.
According to WhyAliyah, the energy shortage weighed heavily on the new state.
According to WhyAliyah, during the period of austerity there was a fuel shortage.
The government forbade heating water between 10:00 and 18:00.
According to Green Prophet, Israel is a small country, and more than half of its land area is desert.
According to the site, it has been a solar energy pioneer almost since the founding of the state in 1948.

stations.title: An engineer's idea, and a prototype at home

paragraphs.text: According to WhyAliyah, engineer Levi Yissar proposed not building more power plants, and switching homes to solar water heaters.
According to WhyAliyah, he built a prototype in his home.
The innovation was a modified electric water heater placed on the roof of the building.
The heater was connected by pipes to two simple glass-faced collector plates.
The water was heated in the collectors and returned by gravity to the insulated heater.
There it was stored for use in kitchens and bathrooms.
According to Green Prophet, all of this happened long before photovoltaic cells and panels were invented.

stations.title: Neryah, and the wait for a heater

paragraphs.text: According to Green Prophet, in 1953 Yissar founded the Neryah Company, the first company to sell such devices.
According to WhyAliyah, NerYah was Israel's first commercial manufacturer of solar water heaters.
According to Green Prophet, the heater became so popular that people waited weeks to buy one.
Improved versions of the heater included an auxiliary electric heating element, to heat water at night or on cloudy days.

stations.title: Cheap oil, and then a law

paragraphs.text: According to WhyAliyah, cheap oil from Iran and from the oil fields captured in the Six-Day War made electricity cheaper, and demand for solar water heaters dropped.
According to WhyAliyah, in 1980 the Knesset passed a law requiring the installation of solar water heaters in every new home.
High towers without enough roof area were excluded from the law.
According to WhyAliyah, by the early 1990s the government already required a solar water-heating system in every new residential building.
According to WhyAliyah, as a result of the mandatory regulations, over 1.3 million solar water heaters are installed in Israel.

stations.title: Zvi Tabor and today's solar water heater

paragraphs.text: According to IFCJ, Harry Zvi Tabor was born to a Jewish family in London and took part in Zionist youth organizations.
According to IFCJ, in 1949 Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion sent a letter to England offering Tabor a job with Israel's Research Council.
According to IFCJ, Tabor founded the National Physical Laboratory of Israel, which, he said, the new state needed.
According to IFCJ, Tabor's heater became the international standard for solar water heating, and helped spread the technology in the United States in the 1970s.
According to IFCJ, Tabor, an Israeli physicist, brought Israel's solar energy program to international prominence.
According to Green Prophet, in 2009 most private homes and small apartment buildings in Israel had solar water heaters.
According to WhyAliyah, in 2007 Israel was the world leader in the use of solar energy per capita, at 3% of primary national energy consumption.
According to WhyAliyah, the Ministry of National Infrastructures estimates that solar water heating saves Israel 2 million barrels of oil a year.
According to Green Prophet, Israeli companies began exporting the heater, mainly to Mediterranean countries such as Greece, Turkey and Italy.
According to Green Prophet, in 2009 Jordan had more than 200,000 collectors, many of them bought from Israel.
According to Green Prophet, that same year Egypt had more than 500,000 solar collectors.
According to Green Prophet, 110,000 devices were installed in Tunisia with the assistance of the Global Environment Facility (GEF).
According to Green Prophet, the solar water heater is also widely used in many homes in the USA, Australia and other countries.
According to Green Prophet, Levi Yissar invented the solar water heater in the early 1950s.
A commenter on the Cleantechies website wrote that Yissar can be given credit for a good design, but the invention predates him by at least one hundred years.
According to the same comment, solar water heaters were in common use in Florida in the 1920s, before the electric company Fla Power & Light offered cheap power.
The commenter also wrote that the water in a solar water heater does not boil, so the English name sun boiler is misleading.
According to a commenter, the efficiency of solar water heaters today averages 40-60%, and it would be good to improve it.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, יששר, מהנדס ויזם, הקים ב-1953 את חברת נריה, החברה הראשונה שמכרה התקנים כאלה.
claims.quote: Yissar, an engineer, and entrepreneur, soon opened the first company selling such devices, the Neryah Company, in 1953.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, הקרדיט על כך מגיע לחלוץ ולממציא הישראלי לוי יששר, שהגה כי אפשר לרתום את כוח השמש.
claims.quote: The credit for much of this can be given to Israeli pioneer innovator Levi Yissar, who had the idea that the sun’s power could be harnessed

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, בתקופת הצנע של שנות ה-50 היה מחסור בדלק, והממשלה אסרה חימום מים בין 10:00 ל-18:00.
claims.quote: During the period of austerity in Israel in the 1950s, there was a fuel shortage, and the government forbade heating water between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, יששר בנה אב-טיפוס בביתו וב-1953 הקים את חברת נריה, היצרנית המסחרית הראשונה של דודי שמש בישראל.
claims.quote: He built a prototype in his home, and in 1953 he started NerYah Company, Israel’s first commercial manufacturer of solar water heaters.

claims.text: החידוש של יששר היה דוד חשמל מותאם שהוצב על גג בניין וחובר בצינורות לשני לוחות קולטים פשוטים עם חזית זכוכית.
claims.quote: His innovation consisted of a modified electric water boiler that was erected on the roof of a building and attached by pipes to two simple glass faced collector plates

claims.text: המים המחוממים חזרו בכוח הכבידה אל הדוד המבודד, ושם אוחסנו לשימוש במטבחים ובחדרי רחצה.
claims.quote: The heated water then returned by gravity feed to the insulated boiler, where it was stored for later use in kitchens and bathrooms.

claims.text: ב-2009, לפי Green Prophet, לתושבי רוב הבתים הפרטיים ובנייני הדירות הקטנים בישראל היו דודי שמש מותקנים.
claims.quote: residents of most private dwellings or smaller apartment buildings in Israel have these sun boilers installed

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, עד אמצע שנות ה-60 אחד מכל 20 משקי בית כבר החזיק דוד שמש, ונמכרו יותר מ-50,000.
claims.quote: By the mid 1960’s, one in every 20 households already had their own sun boiler, and more than 50,000 had been sold.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, עד 1967 אחד מכל עשרים משקי בית חימם מים בשמש ונמכרו 50,000 דודי שמש.
claims.quote: By 1967 around one in twenty households heated its water with the sun and 50,000 solar heaters had been sold.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, ב-1980 העבירה הכנסת חוק המחייב התקנת דודי שמש בכל הבתים החדשים, למעט מגדלים גבוהים ללא שטח גג מספיק.
claims.quote: in 1980 the Israeli Knesset passed a law requiring the installation of solar water heaters in all new homes (except high towers with insufficient roof area)

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, מותקנים בישראל למעלה מ-1.3 מיליון דודי שמש כתוצאה מתקנות חובה להתקנתם.
claims.quote: There are over 1.3 million solar water heaters installed as a result of mandatory solar water heating regulations.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet (2009), דוד השמש הומצא על ידי לוי יששר בתחילת שנות ה-50, כשהחשמל היה יקר מאוד בגלל מחסור חמור באנרגיה.
claims.quote: was invented by a guy named Levi Yissar back in the early 1950’s, when electricity was very expensive due to a severe energy shortage.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, השימוש באנרגיית שמש בישראל החל בשנות ה-50 עם פיתוח דוד שמש על ידי לוי יששר, כדי להתמודד עם מחסור באנרגיה שהכביד על המדינה החדשה.
claims.quote: The use of solar energy began in Israel in the 1950s with the development by Levi Yissar of a solar water heater to address the energy shortages that plagued the new country.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, ישראל, מדינה קטנה של 7 מיליון תושבים שיותר ממחצית שטחה מדבר, היא חלוצה באנרגיית שמש כמעט מאז קום המדינה ב-1948.
claims.quote: Israel, a small country of 7 million, with more than half its land area being desert, has been a solar energy pioneer virtually since its beginning in 1948.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, המהנדס לוי יששר הציע שבמקום להקים עוד תחנות כוח חשמליות, הבתים יעברו לדודי שמש.
claims.quote: As the situation worsened, engineer Levi Yissar proposed that instead of the construction of more electrical generation plants, homes should switch to solar water heaters.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, כל זה התרחש הרבה לפני המצאת תאי ולוחות פוטו-וולטאיים.
claims.quote: all of this came into being long before the invention of photovoltaic solar energy cells and panels (PV)

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, ההתקן הפך פופולרי עד כדי כך שאנשים המתינו שבועות כדי לרכוש דוד שמש.
claims.quote: The device soon became so popular that people waited for weeks to purchase their own

claims.text: גרסאות משופרות כללו התקן חימום חשמלי עזר לחימום מים בלילה או בימים מעוננים.
claims.quote: More modified versions included an auxiliary electric heating device to heat water at night or on cloudy days.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, נפט זול מאיראן ומשדות נפט שנכבשו במלחמת ששת הימים הוזיל את החשמל בישראל, והביקוש לדודי שמש ירד.
claims.quote: However, cheap oil from Iran and from oil fields captured in the Six-Day War made Israeli electricity cheaper and the demand for solar heaters dropped.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, מתחילת שנות ה-90 הממשלה חייבה התקנת מערכות סולאריות לחימום מים בכל בניין מגורים חדש.
claims.quote: As of the early 1990s, all new residential buildings were required by the government to install solar water-heating systems

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, הארי צבי טבור נולד למשפחה יהודית בלונדון והשתתף בארגוני נוער ציוניים.
claims.quote: Born to a Jewish family in London, Tabor participated in Zionist Youth organizations.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, ב-1949 שלח ראש הממשלה דוד בן-גוריון מכתב לאנגליה והציע לטבור משרה במועצת המחקר של ישראל.
claims.quote: Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion sent a letter to England offering Tabor a job with the “physics and engineering desk” of Israel’s Research Council.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, טבור הקים בישראל את המעבדה הפיזיקלית הלאומית, שלדבריו המדינה החדשה הייתה זקוקה לה.
claims.quote: Tabor created the National Physical Laboratory of Israel, which he knew the new nation needed.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, במשבר הנפט של שנות ה-70 פיתח הארי צבי טבור את אב-הטיפוס של דוד השמש המשמש כיום ביותר מ-90% מהבתים בישראל.
claims.quote: With the 1970s oil crisis, Harry Zvi Tabor developed the prototype of the solar water heater now used in over 90% of Israeli homes.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, טבור פיתח את דוד השמש שבו משתמשים 95% ממשקי הבית בישראל.
claims.quote: Tabor developed the solar water heater used by 95% of Israeli households.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, הדוד של טבור הפך לסטנדרט הבינלאומי לחימום מים סולארי ועזר להפיץ את הטכנולוגיה התרמית-סולארית בארה"ב בשנות ה-70.
claims.quote: This became the international standard for solar water heating, and helped popularize solar thermal technology in the United States in the 1970s.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, טבור, פיזיקאי ישראלי, הביא את תוכנית האנרגיה הסולארית של ישראל לבולטות בינלאומית.
claims.quote: An Israeli physicist, Tabor brought Israel’s solar energy program to international prominence.

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, ב-2007 ישראל הייתה המובילה בעולם בשימוש באנרגיית שמש לנפש (3% מצריכת האנרגיה הלאומית הראשונית).
claims.quote: Israel was in 2007 the world leader in the use of solar energy per capita (3% of the primary national energy consumption).

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, משרד התשתיות הלאומיות מעריך שחימום מים בשמש חוסך לישראל 2 מיליון חביות נפט בשנה.
claims.quote: The Ministry of National Infrastructures estimates solar water heating saves Israel 2 million barrels (320,000 m3) of oil a year.

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, חברות ישראליות החלו לייצא את ההתקן, בעיקר למדינות הים התיכון כמו יוון, טורקיה ואיטליה.
claims.quote: Israeli companies also began exporting the device, particularly to other Mediterranean countries such as Greece, Turkey and Italy.

claims.text: ב-2009, לפי Green Prophet, בירדן יש יותר מ-200,000 קולטים, רבים מהם נרכשו מישראל.
claims.quote: Jordan has more than 200,000, many of them purchased from Israel.

claims.text: ב-2009, לפי Green Prophet, במצרים יש יותר מ-500,000 קולטי שמש, והיא וירדן משתמשות בשיטה זו.
claims.quote: Middle Eastern countries like Jordan and Egypt, which has more than 500,000 solar collectors, are also availing themselves

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, גם בטוניסיה הותקנו 110,000 התקנים בסיוע קרן הסביבה העולמית (GEF).
claims.quote: And even North African countries like Tunisia have also gotten into the act (110,000) with the assistance of the Global Environment Facility (GEF)

claims.text: לפי Green Prophet, דוד השמש עדיין בשימוש רב, גם בבתים רבים בארה"ב, באוסטרליה ובמדינות אחרות.
claims.quote: The old “dude shemesh” is still very much in use, however, even in many homes in the USA, Australia, and other countries.

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, אפשר לתת ליששר קרדיט על תכנון טוב, אך ההמצאה של דוד השמש קודמת לו בלפחות מאה שנה.
claims.quote: While credit can be given to Levi Yissar for a good design, the invention of the dude shemesh dates at least one hundred years earlier.

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, דודי שמש היו בשימוש נפוץ בפלורידה בשנות ה-20, לפני שחברת החשמל Fla Power & Light הציעה חשמל זול.
claims.quote: They were in common use in Florida in the 1920’s before Fla Power & Light came in with cheap power.

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, המים אינם רותחים בדוד שמש, ולכן המונח "דוד שמש" באנגלית (sun boiler) מטעה.
claims.quote: The water doers not boil in a dude shemesh so using the term “subn boiler” is misleading.

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, היעילות הנוכחית של דודי שמש היא בממוצע 40-60%, ורצוי לשפרה.
claims.quote: Higher efficiency would be appreciated (they are currently averaging 40-60%)

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, לישראל יש הצפיפות הגבוהה בעולם של דודי שמש וקפריסין שנייה.
claims.quote: Israel has the highest density of solar water heaters in the world (Cyprus is second).

claims.text: לפי WhyAliyah, ישראל וקפריסין מובילות לנפש בשימוש במערכות מים חמים סולאריות, ובהן משתמשים מעל 90% מהבתים.
claims.quote: Israel and Cyprus are the per-capita leaders in the use of solar hot water systems with over 90% of homes using them.

claims.text: לפי תגובת גולש, סין היא המדינה מספר אחת בדודי שמש.
claims.quote: Just come and have a look in China, number one solar water heater country, Edouard.
